# Fixed accountable Frank local-review results

Status: accepted bounded implementation, component-validated on the physical Mac; actual Frank/normal-binary/receiver integration and installed admission remain open. The fixed contract `8ed036a4328a240abd4d5012d02ed9820d9226f45601a0b4d88e022e52981129` and independent review `c05fc61037f67c0f61686dff39880bed42a2fd3bb7b4fffb2e10efea5b469818` remain binding. No live role or Application is enabled by source validation.

The fixed authority accepts responsibility for an exact retained effect-disabled local-review computation. It does not prove source truth, independent software execution, current Runtime Attempt freshness, owner approval or external mutation. Frank's actual final claim check and Runtime's lease/fence/retired Attempt checks retain their responsibilities. Same-owner full-state rollback or an owner able to replace every private source is not isolated by this implementation.

## API and wire

`FrankResultAuthority::open_pinned_owner_configuration(path, [u8;32])` hashes the same bounded private configuration bytes consumed before parsing. `execute(FrankResultMode::{Attest,Resume,Renew}, exact_selector)` returns only the existing `frank.secs-result-envelope.v1` bytes. The normal `secs-frank-result` binary accepts exactly `<attest|resume|renew> --config <owner path> --config-sha256 <64 lowercase hex>`, reads at most1,024 stdin bytes, writes exact retained stdout bytes with no framing newline, and emits one fixed denial on stderr. Paths and hash are trusted composition, never model or remote request data. Transport supervision remains the caller's responsibility.

Selector is closed `{schema:frank.result-capture-selector.v1,capture_id,renewal_of}` with explicit null for the original issue. Attest creates once. Resume is exact-byte no-create recovery, including after lost output; expired or missing state denies. Renew explicitly names the previous exact envelope hash and creates one new edge for the identical capture. It authenticates the old body/signature/current owners without requiring the old window to remain live. There is no denied-issue fallback or provider execution.

Packet v0, schema4 context and Frank work/result payloads remain unchanged. Audience is `frank://result-receiver`, operation `frank.result.attest.v1`, resource is the full run/step/Attempt/effect path. The full existing `OperationDescriptor` is fixed to this meaning and its `descriptor:sha256:` digest is projected as raw64 only after exact validation. Opcode/handler remain owner-selected; fixture231 is not an allocation. Runtime|Service Application, ServiceAuthority, existing journal, registry rows, generic Wallet signing and the verification helper are unchanged.

## Private sources and real observations

The configuration is the closed schema recorded in the accepted contract: issuer root/subject/key/public key, assignment root+hash, capture root, journal root, descriptor and maximum_ttl. The owner assignment fixes actor/integration/route, at most64 explicit run IDs, at most9 canonical review operations, generation/window and producer/normalizer/composition/source-manifest hashes. `configuration_sha256` in a capture is the producer-composition configuration, not this Native startup file; there is no assignment hash cycle.

Reuse `IssuerDirectory` and its held seed/lock/root custody. The current owner assignment is the key-validity window because the raw issuer seed has no independent expiry record; no second expiry database is invented. Frank's current public-key and subject policy separately imposes receiver bounds. Assignment/config/capture/lock/key identities and bytes are revalidated under retained cooperative locks after blocking operations and SQLite close. Actual SystemTime supplies a sticky operation clock and a durable authenticated high-water floor. Issued time is sampled after current owners and entropy; final export repeats current ownership and exclusive ≤60-second window admission. This is local cooperative publication and rollback detection, not global revocation or network time.

Capture layout, agreed with the Frank producer:

- `capture_root/source-manifest.json`, `capture.lock`, `blobs/<sha256>`.
- `capture_root/<sha256(exact reservation.json)>/{reservation.json,work.json,payload.json,receipt.json}`.
- Reservation: closed schema, reservation_id, work_sha256, configuration_sha256.
- Source manifest: closed schema, producer_artifact_sha256, normalizer_sha256, configuration_sha256 and unique `{sha256,byte_length}` entries containing all three pinned composition blobs.
- Receipt: exact accepted capture fields, ordered actual observations and completion code; each observation is `{kind,input_sha256,output_sha256,byte_length,reference}`. Explicit null is required for an inapplicable hash. Reference selects the output hash when present, otherwise input hash. Both resolve to retained bytes or exact work bytes. The last observation is an actual claim-check with input equal to work hash and a retained output. No fake provider response or fabricated work-read is added for pure transformations.

The seven accepted observation kinds are unchanged. Known failed handlers may retain an actual artifact return whose content did not match the requested port reference; Native verifies the recorded bytes' own hash, not an assertion that the failed artifact check succeeded. Work/reservation and payload/receipt supply the real input and completion records. Native does not rerun handlers or inspect external providers. Frank must publish an immutable directory only after its durable completed row and recover a publication failure from the exact stored bytes, without computation again.

Successful captures additionally require the actual ordered non-claim port trace for their fixed operation: load-review reads audio/events; transcription reads audio then records the transcription response over those exact bytes; component resolution records the subject/events query; annotation and extraction record their actual artifact writes; source binding records one subject/selectors query per observation (zero for zero observations); final review reads its input packet and records packet/note writes; status reads packet/note and records its exact simulated status intent; daily-note reads transcript/note and records its exact simulated daily-note intent. Successful artifact references must equal the actual returned write reference and the content hash/length of its retained input bytes. All claim-check inputs bind the exact work; their real outputs remain opaque retained observations, including historical null, not an invented boolean assertion. This validates accountable call/evidence relationships, not a second execution of timing, normalization, source or semantic policy. Known failed prefixes skip success-only obligations and may retain genuinely mismatching artifact returns without fabricated provider/write calls.

Bounds are local fail-closed ceilings: work1MiB; native payload256KiB; configuration/assignment64KiB; receipt/reservation/source manifest16KiB each;128 observations/manifest entries; evidence1MiB per blob; selected manifest≤128 such blobs; trace≤4MiB counting every input/output occurrence, including repeats. Held unique evidence is consequently≤132MiB. No public Runtime or artifact limit is widened. Oversize selected inputs deny rather than truncate. Body parsing retains original numeric lexemes, supports finite floats/wide integers and depth64, rejects duplicate keys/nonfinite values, and never reserializes signed work/result/payload. Only newly constructed metadata gets a sorted-key serializer independent of hostile serde map features.

## Durable private ledger

Only fixed `journal.lock`, `journal.initialized`, `results.sqlite3` and SQLite's fixed DELETE journal are allowed. The original private root/lock/DB identities remain bound. An instance opened before another bootstrap must adopt the exact marker bytes and identity under the journal lock before accepting that existing database. Every physical/final check requires the already-bound database to remain present with the same inode, including when directory enumeration omits a deleted entry. Initialization is create-only and marks a new DB; partial bootstrap or a missing DB with a marker denies, not recovery from a proof. No automatic repair, pruning or eviction exists.

All states count: at most32 capture rows and32 attestation rows,32MiB logical complete row bytes,16 generations per capture. DB pages cap at8,192×4,096 (32MiB), DELETE journal≤33MiB and aggregate physical charge≤65MiB. Capacity denies while preserving original identity. The private snapshot uses Ed25519 over fixed domain `frank.result.private-ledger.v1\0`, startup configuration hash and SHA256 of the canonical complete rows plus durable clock floor. It is not a raw public signer, secret-prefix MAC or new transport wire. Every read verifies the snapshot, all capture and original byte bindings, canonical signed outputs/signatures, unique selectors/replay IDs, complete one-root renewal chains and floor≥every issuance. Edited/deleted rows or a lowered floor cannot silently reopen an effect. Entire old-directory rollback remains outside the stated owner trust boundary.

Commit and close uncertainty never returns success. An audited failed operation attempts to retain its observed clock floor after rollback without replacing the primary denial. A successful output requires a final current-owner check after close; any later advancing clock is durably sealed before another final check. The old original result remains immutable through explicit renewal.
